answer.evidence: The running head 'THEOSOPHY FOR THE PROFANE. 115' is at the top of the leaf. Its first line is 'shrillest sounds, and in our brain there will be silence', and its last line is 'plane of which that spirit is the rightful denizen. And higher yet, till he'. The heading 'The Building of Man.' is in the middle of the page.

Opens with 'Illuminatus, acutus ingeniosus' directly under the 'Latina.' heading at the top of the leaf; closes with 'Coetaneus, contubernalis' at the bottom; the page number 85 is printed in the top-right corner next to 'Arabica.'

The opening line 'denied nothing, he evidently declined to talk about that matter' is at the top of leaf p312, under the header '308 LUCIFER.' The closing line 'And those who, perchance, may believe are . . . as likely' is at the bottom of the same leaf. Leaf p311 (folio 307) ends with 'But, though he', which leads straight into this text, and leaf p313 (folio 309) continues with 'as not to attribute these manifestations'.

Opens 'nia animalia, habent appetitum naturalem eorum quæ alunt' at top of left column and has 'CAPUT XI. Ex quibus partibus componitur anima' midway down the right column, which ends 'primas autem essentia-'. Leaf p217 has the header 'LIBER II DE ANIMA, TRACT. I 209' and signature 'v'. Leaf p218 (printed 210) instead begins 'les. In spiritualibus autem dicimus'.

The title page of p41 runs from "MYSTERIUM MAGNUM, Oder Erklärung über das Erste Buch Mosis/" at the top to "Zu Amsterdam/ Gedruckt im Jahr Christi 1682." at the bottom, with the printer's ornament in between. p42 is only the blank back of that leaf, with show-through and a 'MADE AND PRINTED IN HOLLAND' stamp.

The transcription's header '398 LUCIFER.' matches the running head on this leaf. Its first line, 'I am wearied with my heart's imagining of its own excess.', is the first line here. It ends with '(To be continued.)', an ornament and 'Pagodas are measured by their shadows... (Chinese Aphorisms.)', which are at the bottom of this leaf.

Transcription opens with 'Holem uuc. | Holhucakal. | 5 fois 7. | 35' and ends with 'Un million, deux millions, trois millions, etc. … Hunkinchil, ca kinchil, ox kinchil, etc.'. Leaf p157 has the same first table row at the top and the same last line at the bottom. It also has the header 'GRAMMAIRE ET CHRESTOMATHIE. 99' and the signature '13.' at the foot. Leaf p158 is blank and shows only bleed-through from the other side.

The transcription opens with 'The Banshee (Sean-sidhe) seems to be one of the sociable fairies', the first line under the '404 LUCIFER.' header on leaf p408. It ends with 'vapour of Domnian Titanism. W. B. YEATS! (To be continued.)', which matches the signature and closing note at the bottom of that leaf.

The transcription's header 'REVIEWS, 523' and its first line 'But there is one caution which should be observed by all readers' match the top of leaf p527. Its last lines, ending '7, Duke Street, Adelphi, London.', match the bottom of the Theosophical News section on the same leaf.

The header 'Arabica. 111' matches the top right of the leaf. The first entry 'Arator.' sits at the top of the Latin column, and the last entry 'Combustor fordium, stabularius.' sits at the bottom. The catchword 'ⲡⲓϥⲟⲙ' is in the lower right.
The transcription's 'Illi mutuo, inuicem' matches the first line under the header on leaf 511, which is printed page 455. Its last entry, 'Pastor', matches the last line on the same leaf.

Opens 'the ford which we must pass. Twenty of the cavalry were also to patrole' at the top of leaf p220 (folio 196) and ends 'I must now remind you how we have' at its foot. The transcription's page-num 196 matches; p221 is folio 197 and opens 'have written to his Majesty'.

The transcription begins with the running head 'ACCURSED. 315' and the line 'think of it ; that owing to your revengeful feelings'. These are at the top of leaf 319. It ends with 'twisted it into one formless mass. It was dislodged and hanging down', which is the last line of that leaf.

The transcription opens with 'Caput XXV. quintum, et vigesimum' followed by 'Consolatio'. It ends with 'Iteratio, repetitio.' and the catchword 'EZDH'. Leaf 284 matches this: it is printed page 228, with the same heading at the top of the Latin column and the same last entry and catchword at the bottom.

The transcription begins 'preserving the traditions of Indian painting almost intact in Rajputana' and ends 'a realistic embodiment of their chosen deity. As'. Those are the first and last lines of leaf p70, which has the header '50 INDIAN PAINTING'. Leaf p71 is folio 51 and begins 'a consequence, the plastic arts predominated'.

The transcription starts with section heading 'IX LES KABBALISTES ONT-ILS PROFESSÉ LE SYSTÈME ASTRONOMIQUE D'ARISTARQUE DE SAMOS ?' and ends with 'A reconnaître, dans ce passage, une allusion à la rotation diurne' plus notes 1–5 (Franck, Pauly, Zohar III fol. 16a). These match the top, bottom line and footnotes of leaf p153, folio 143. Leaf p154 is folio 144 and starts 'de la Terre, nous serons moins disposés qu'Ad. Franck'.

The transcription starts with 'we predict the course of life whether even or rugged' under the header '390 LUCIFER.' at the top of p402. It ends with 'died there as the astrologer had foretold.', which is the last line of the same leaf.

The transcription opens with 'Pascha.' and 'Eloquentia, facundia', which are the first entries at the top of the leaf headed 'Arabica. 283'. It closes with 'Blasphemia, vituperium' on the last line, which sits just above the signature 'Nn 2' at the foot of the page.

The running head 'OCCULT AXIOMS AND THEIR SYMBOLS. 425' matches. The first line, 'that competition is one of the springs of material progress', is at the top of leaf p429. The last line, 'them altogether to eternal perdition; and if you protest, he will damn you too.', is at the bottom of that leaf.

The transcription opens with "comme le veut l'Épinomide, n'est pas, pour les astres errants" and ends with "que le système de Platon ne sauvait pas." Both lines match the top and bottom of the text on leaf p128, which has the printed folio 116 and the header LA COSMOLOGIE HELLÉNIQUE. That leaf also has the same planetary revolutions table (Vénus to Saturne) and footnote 1, "G. Schiaparelli, loc. cit., p. 152".

The heading 'The Old House in the Canongate' and the opening 'HE after events are very dimly outlined on my mind now' are at the top of the leaf. The last line, 'But it seemed to me that without, or even against his will, the power of his', is at the bottom.

The transcription begins "focal points of the Empire. The Bishop of Rome" and ends "The 'Chair of Peter,'* therefore,". Both lines match the first and last body lines on p100, which carries the printed folio 96. Its footnote, "There appear to have been two chairs of the titular apostle... 1662", sits at the bottom of p100. The leaf labelled p101 (folio 97) starts instead with "is sacred rather than apostolical".

The heading 'The Elixir of the Devil' and 'CHAPTER II.' sit at the top of leaf p383. Its first line is 'WAS sixteen years of age when the parish priest informed me', and its last line, 'liness of the Prior was even heightened when he read the letter, and he', is at the foot of the same leaf. The transcription's header folio '372' is a misread of the printed 379.

The transcription begins "406 LUCIFER. And the Voice said, with tones deep and soft like the Atlantic wave", which matches the running head and first line at the top of leaf p410. It ends with "Maria in the heart of each ?"—Om." and the signature "A. J. C. / Lucerne", which match the bottom of the same leaf.

The transcription runs from "step delicately on roses" at the top of the leaf down to "I have nowhere passed without learning thousands of finer" at the bottom. It also includes Herbert Burrows's signature and the heading "Sir Edwin Arnold on Japanese Buddhism" in the middle of leaf p70, which is printed as page 62.

The transcription begins 'PISTIS-SOPHIA. 393 / with the greatest possible Light, forty and nine* times', which matches the header and top line of leaf 405. It ends with 'them [26] because they knew not the mystery, which was done (3).' The leaf has '[25]' there, an OCR misreading. The four footnotes, starting '* Typical of the "forty-nine fires"', match the foot of the same leaf.

The transcription's header 'FROM THE EAST OF TIME. 395' and its first line 'Onora seems to read my soul; I cannot bear to stand in presence' match the top of leaf p399. Its last line, 'oak. Onora wished to paint, and I wished nothing save to lie upon the', matches that leaf's last line.

The transcription opens with 'uiditur. Altior enim profundiorque, qui κεφαλήν' and ends with 'Sic Hippocrati, libr. de arte,'. Leaf p56 is headed '34 ADRIANI SPIGELII DE HVMANI', starts and ends with the same words, and has 'CAPVT III. De ossium inter se structura ac connexu' in the middle. Leaf p57 is folio 35 and starts with 'arte, ἄρθρα vocantur'.

The transcription opens with 'and there came to a halt. The most respectable matron' and closes with 'A Cornelian gem, with a representation of this cere-'. Both lines match the first and last lines of leaf p194, which has the header '188 GREEK AND ROMAN PHALLISM.'

Transcription opens 'were cursed by the tongue of David,¹ and of Jesus,' and closes 'outstep it ³—'. This matches the top and bottom of the leaf with printed folio 550. The footnotes match too: 'See Sura ii. 61, p. 373; Mark viii. 30', the Geiger note on 'rahiba', and 'Comp. Sura [cix.] lxvi. 2'. Leaf p583 is printed page 551 and starts 'And eat of what God hath given you'.

Transcription opens 'مزاحف هزلى بينها متباعد ❊ وكما قال الآخر' and closes 'فقال بعضنا ينبغي ان' with signature '(11 - حيوان دس)'. These match the first line, last line and footer of leaf p267 (printed 81). Leaf p268 (printed 82) starts with 'يكون مولى هذه الجارية', which continues that text.

Header '842. THEOPOMPUS (OR CRATIPPUS), HELLENICA 167' and opening 'κεδα[ιμον' (line 3 of the leaf); the accented edited text 'τῶν] ἄλλων βαρβάρω[ν' in Fr. 11 matches p183. p182 (folio 166) has the same fragments, but only as an unaccented diplomatic transcript, and p184 (folio 168) shows Col. xi.

The transcription opens with "to the rank of a mighty champion of Belief; therefore let him enter the service of God!", which is the first line of leaf p328. It closes with "which the Princess herself placed in my mouth, taking me upon her lap.", which is the last line of that leaf. The OCR header "324 LOCIFISK:" is a misreading of that leaf's running head, "324 LUCIFER."

The transcription starts with '422 LUCIFER.' and 'and that a few moments of deep love or even bitter emotion are worth three-score years', which matches the header and first lines of leaf p426. It ends with 'We should have very different ideas about motion if we were enclosed in an', which matches the last line of that leaf.

The transcription opens with 'depresso, lam. minus confertis latioribus' and closes with 'In dumetis, pratis silvaticis muscosis'. Both lines appear on leaf p372, first and last line, under the header '352 AGARICINI'. It is not on p373, which is folio 353, headed RUSSULA, and starts with 'freq. Pileo ob pelliculam'.

The transcription opens with 'Percufferunt, direxit, conduxit, ligare' and ends with 'Ambulauit.' plus the catchword 'ⲁⲩⲓ'. On leaf p372, printed page 316, 'Percusserunt, dire-xit,conduxit' is the first entry at the top and 'Ambulauit.' is the last entry at the bottom, followed by the catchword 'ⲁⲩⲓ...'

The transcription begins with "among them, and they cannot differ much either in age or purpose" and ends with "The relative distances of these satellites to their". Both lines match the first and last lines of p173. That leaf also has the header "CHAP. IV. DERBYSHIRE. 147" and the signature "L 2" at the bottom. Leaf p174 is printed page 148 and starts with "primaries is nearly proportional...".

The transcription is marked '<page-type>blank</page-type>' and has no text. Leaf p92 is the only blank leaf among p90–p96. The leaf filed as page 93 has printed text: folio 69, Fig. 9 and the line 'and is the reciprocal of 2.927'. The other leaves all have text or a plate.

Opens 'quam facili iuratione etiam ad periurium cecidisset' at the top of leaf p106 (printed 102, header SANCTI AUGUSTINI VITA). Ends with 'CAPUT XXVI / De convictu feminarum ... usque in diem obitus sui praeposita an-' at the foot of the main text. Leaf p107 is printed 103 and holds the English translation.

The transcription opens with 'Calices, crateres.' and ends with 'Torcular.' followed by the catchword 'No-'. Leaf p502 (printed 446) starts its Latin column with 'Calices,crateres.', ends it with 'Torcular.', and has the catchword 'No-' at the bottom right.
The entries run from "Gomor, 19. modiorum" at the top of the Latin column to "Modius minor continens 15. mensuras" at the bottom of leaf p200, which is printed page 144.

The transcription begins "the past, as mere children; while they themselves have risen as giants" and ends "who put the words "evolution"". Both lines match the first and last lines of leaf p386, which has the header 'LUCIFER.' and the printed folio 374. Leaf p387 is folio 375 and begins with "and "miracle" as flags of opposite camps."

The transcription begins 'having eyes as beautiful as the leaf of the lotos' and ends 'Vasudeva, also called Anakadundubhi, had Pauraví,¹'. These are the first and last lines of the main text on p116, which is printed folio 108 with the header 'VISHNU PURÁNA'. The footnote 'Pauraví is, rather, a title attached to a second Rohiní' also appears at the bottom of p116. Leaf p117 is folio 109 and starts with 'Rohiní, Madirá, Bhadrá, Devakí'.

The transcription is 'blank' with only 'foxing and minor staining'. Two leaves fit that: p204 and p206 are both blank and foxed, and the transcription has no text to tell them apart. p207 is actually a full text page headed 'CARNAC—DESCRIPTION OF PLATES. lxxxvii', so it does not match.

The transcription has no text. It describes a book edge photo with "pages... darkened or stained with age, showing a deep reddish-brown hue" and the leather binding on the left and right. That matches the dark brown edge on p4. The edges on p3 and p5 are bright red/orange, and none of the other leaves shows a book edge.

Opens with "494 LUCIFER. myself to my task and strengthening myself by draughts from the mysterious flask" and has "(To be continued.)" then the heading "IF YOU SHOOT AT A CROW, DO NOT KILL A COW". It ends with "sanctum sanctorum of the eminent European philologist.—[ED.]". All of these appear on leaf p498 (printed 494), from the top of the page to the bottom.

Running head 'Dumu-du-kug and Gibil 203' at the top of leaf 213; text starts '82. The way of whose princely power no god equals.' and the last note reads '⁹ C. 57 II 10. ... See also KING, i 181, 6.' at the bottom of the page. Leaf 214 is printed page 204, Tablet VII, with lines 98–113 in transliteration.

The transcription is the first page of the table of contents: it opens with 'TABLE DES MATIÈRES DU TOME IV', then Chapitre VIII ('L'École de Paris et le système de Ptolémée ... 3') and Chapitre IX ('Jean Buridan ... 124'). None of these leaves carries that text. p607 (folio 597) is the last table-of-contents page, covering the Néo-platonisme arabe and Averroès chapters (402–584). p608–p612 are blank endpapers, and p613 is the back cover with the Wellesley library label.

The transcription starts with the heading 'Skaldatal/ Deter: Fortegnelse paa de fornemste Skaldrer' and ends with 'Svend Alfivasøn. { Thorar Loftunga.' On p895 the same heading is at the top, the same line is at the bottom, and the signature reads 'Krrrr 3'. The printed page carries no page number. p896 starts instead with 'Thorleikur Fagre' and 'Hellig Knud'.

The transcription begins 'As yet, however, we seem to have been only contemplating the lesser mysteries' and ends 'progress of the British ceremony', with the footnote 'Plut. in Vita Phor.' This matches the leaf for p239 from top to bottom. Its printed folio is 237.

The transcription only says '(This page is blank.)'. Pages 518 and 520 are both blank and look the same, so it could be either. Page 521 itself is not blank: it has 'TABLE DES MATIÈRES DU TOME PREMIER'.

The transcription opens with 'Lune des orbites capables de remplir une telle condition' and ends with 'L'ensemble des orbes d'un astre'. Leaf p103 starts and ends with the same lines. Its printed folio is 93, it has the Fig. 14 diagram, and its footnote reads 'Ptolémée, Op. laud., éd. cit., pp. 138-141'. Leaf p104 is folio 94 and starts 'errant, de Saturne par exemple'.

The running head "64 LUCIFER." and the heading "The First Step." are at the top of the leaf. The text ends with "in social intercourse, and so forth. Let the last half" in the last line at the bottom.

The transcription opens with "man, we turned towards the adored interpreter" and ends with the footnote "The Spirit seems to forget the millions of the 'heathen'". On leaf p525 the first line sits right under the running head "THE LETTERS OF JOHANN CASPAR LAVATER. 513", and the footnote is the last line at the bottom of the page.

The heading 'PRALAYA' and the first line 'The Light-Born spoke unto the Dark-Born say-ing:' are at the top of leaf p52. The last line 'The veil itself an unreality.' sits just above the folio 44. Leaf p53 (folio 45) is a different poem, 'CONSCIOUSNESS'.

The transcription's header "388 LUCIFER.", heading "GRAPHOLOGY." and first line "VERY physical action of the human body" match the top of leaf p392. Its last line, "the fiery furnace of worldly desires and passions before it can be said", matches the bottom line of the same leaf.

The transcription opens with 'Nomina Mensium Arabum', 'Annus eorum 365 dies' and 'Almuharan, respondet Septembri', and closes with 'Feria Sexta' and 'Sabbatum.' Leaf p121 has the same opening at the top of the Latin column, the same closing at the bottom, and the folio number 65 in the top right corner.

The transcription's first entry, 'Apostolica', matches the first line under the column headings, next to the folio number 304. Its last entry, 'Ioppe civitas Palaestinae', matches the final entry at the foot of the page.

The transcription opens with 'any known obligation to family, kindred or country', the first line on leaf p25 under the header 'INTRODUCTION. 17'. It ends with 'let freedom of the', the last line on that leaf. Leaf p26 is folio 18 and begins 'soul in the light of science'.

Starts 'souverain Bien par une marche compliquée...', has heading 'XVI LA PLURALITÉ DES MONDES', and ends 'Ainsi le lieu naturel du feu est la région qui se trouve immédia-'. All of this matches leaf p242 (folio 230) from top to bottom, including notes 1–2 (De Cœlo lib. I, cap. IX / cap. VIII). Leaf p243 is folio 231 and starts 'tement au-dessous de l'orbe de la Lune'.

Opens 'and all the Houses of their Spheres, and all the Orders of each one of them.' at the top of leaf p118 (printed 110, LUCIFER header), and its notes end with '(8) The distinction between lux and lumen' at the bottom.

The first row, 'Rex pacis, Rex iustitiae.', is at the top of the Latin column on the leaf printed 222, and the last row, 'Moses, extractus.', is at the bottom. The catchword 'ⲁⲁⲣⲟⲛ' is in the lower right, and the next leaf (223) begins with Aaron.

The transcription opens with "30. modios, & modius 3. & ephe 3. mensuras minutas" and ends with "Situla, vas ex corio fectum ad hauriendam aquam." These match the top and bottom of the Latin column on the leaf headed "Arabica, 149". The heading "Nomina Instrumentorum, seu suppellectilium" is in the middle of the same leaf.

The transcription is marked '<page-type>blank</page-type>' with no text. Leaf p132 is the only blank leaf in the set: plain toned paper with no text. It sits between the Al-Kindi notation plate (p131) and printed page 109 (p133). The other six leaves all have printed text or the plate. Calling it a 'flyleaf or endpaper' is wrong, since this is the blank back of a plate inside the book. A blank page carries no text to compare, so the match rests only on p132 being the one blank leaf here.

The transcription begins with the running head '136 LUCIFER.' and the line 'i. pp. III, 112), is the "constructive power"'. It ends with 'and so onwards, with races, worlds, systems,'. Leaf p144 has the same folio 136 and the same first and last lines.

The transcription starts with 'SCENE VII. FIGARO, CHÉRUBIN, LA COMTESSE, SUZANNE.' at the top of the left column on leaf p44 (printed folio 42). It ends with '...il reçoit le plus rude soufflet, et s'enfuit en éclatant de rire.' at the bottom of the right column of the same leaf.

The transcription opens with 'Hoc Latinū fecit ille, qui in Græca epigrammata annotationes confcripfit', which is the first line under the header '628 Vlyfsis Aldrouandi' on leaf p644. It has the same 'VSVS IN MEDICINA.' heading with the ornamental 'A' in the middle of the page, and it ends with the catchword 'ter pe-' at the bottom right. Leaf p645 is folio 629 and opens with 'ter pedibus terram attingat'.

The running head 'xxviii INTRODUCTORY NOTICE' matches. So does the opening line 'mission in 1247, and had there met this same David at the camp of Baidju', at the top of the leaf. The text closes with 'but also one to the Emperor of the Mongols,' and footnote 3 'William of Nangis, 360, 361.' sits at the bottom.

The transcription starts 'even distinguish between the two seers of grain', which is the first line under the header '428 LUCIFER.' on leaf p432. It ends with 'AMARAVELLA.' and the ERRATA list ('302, 36, for Aarzoo, read Aanroo') at the bottom of the same leaf.

The transcription opens with 'topics of Karma, Re-incarnation, ‘The Wonder Light’', which is the first line of the leaf under the 'THEOSOPHICAL ACTIVITIES. 523' running head. It closes with 'withdraw his own followers from the Section and break it up.', which is the last line at the bottom of the same leaf.

The transcription opens with "is lost in the radiance of Atma, and becomes consciously one with the All." That is the first line of the leaf with the folio 116 and the running head LUCIFER. It ends with "how they supposed a man could sin ere yet he was born, but were answered:", which is the last line of the same leaf.

The transcription is '<page-type>blank</page-type> ... This page is a blank flyleaf or endpaper'. Of the seven leaves, only p518 is blank (it is the back of the plate 'Dr. Johnson's House, Bolt Court, Fleet Street' on p517). The other leaves are text pages 490–494 or the plate itself; p519 is printed page 491, 'The use of entails'.

Folio 280 with the 'WAS HE MAD? (Concluded from the November Number.)' heading. The leaf opens with '. . . As he spoke, a heavy book that was lying on the table rose' and ends with '"It is only as I feared," said the Professor, after I had become restored.' The p285 leaf (folio 281) starts with '"The sudden disclosing...' instead.

The running head "FROM THE EAST OF TIME. 473" is at the top of the leaf. The title and "By CHARLES HANNAN" follow. The text opens "T seems strange that the world should be moving onwards" and ends at the bottom with "I laugh with a great happiness at my own folly when I", followed by the signature mark 33.
The header 'Arabica. 279' matches the top right of leaf 335. Its first entry, 'Aduentus Domini.', is at the top of the Latin column, and its last entry, 'Forum, Plateæ,', is at the bottom.

The transcription begins with "series of musical fêtes were held for three days" and ends with "seeing that Ja‘far al-Ṣādiq (d. 765)". These are the first and last body lines of leaf p97, which has the header "THE UMAYYADS 75". Its two footnotes (Encyclopædia of Islām, i, 1012; the dates of ‘Azza al-Mailā’...) also match. Leaf p98 is printed page 76 and begins "the sixth imām".

The transcription says only that the page is "blank, with only faint, illegible traces of text showing through." That doesn't fit p303 itself, which has pasted catalogue clippings ("Catullus, Tibullus... SYLVAE... M.CCCCLX") and a handwritten note ("Waterstained, and some wormholes, but complete with the 2 blank leaves. Bernard Quaritch"). The description could fit several leaves equally well: p300 has faint show-through text, p301 has a faint show-through stamp, and p302 and p304 are blank. So the transcription can't be tied to one leaf.
Opens with the heading 'Fæminina. ... Masculina.' and the entry 'Vulpes.' at the top of the leaf. Closes with 'Palmus, cubitus.' at the bottom. The header 'Arabica. 253' is at the top right.

The transcription begins with the running head "THEOSOPHICAL AND MYSTIC PUBLICATIONS. 87" and "IN THE THEOSOPHIST for January and February", which is the top of the left column on leaf p95 under the decorative heading. It ends with "we wish it had not been," which is the bottom of the right column on the same leaf.

The transcription is only "blank page" and has no text. Pages 611 and 612 are blank endpapers, and page 614 is the plain red cloth back cover, so all three fit equally well. Only page 613 is ruled out, because it has a Wellesley College Library barcode and a 'Duhem. Le système du monde' card pocket.

The transcription says '<page-type>blank</page-type>' and 'no legible text or imagery present'. That doesn't fit p141, which is printed page lv and opens 'person also at hand to mark that no ceremony or circumstance should be omitted'. p138 (only faint show-through) and p140 are both blank, so there's no way to tell which of the two it renders. p139 is the 'No 29 Botallek Circles' plate, and p142–p144 are text pages lvi–lviii.

The transcription opens with 'Dux belli.', which is the first entry under the 'Latina.' heading at the top of page 162. It ends with 'Locus præfecti, curatoris.', the last entry at the bottom of that leaf. The page number 106 is printed at the top left.

The transcription begins "qu'il est né. Lorsqu'il a un an il se répand" and ends "comme la bête". Both lines are on p519, which has the header "VENDIDAD. FARG. XIII.", folio 385, signature Ccc and footnote [1] "Soné éeoûé héefchtâ befrém". Leaf 522 is folio 388 and has different text.
